docs.title: danaSeq
docs.text: Metagenomic and amplicon analysis pipelines for Oxford Nanopore and Illumina sequencing data. Six independent Nextflow DSL2 pipelines cover real-time read classification, long-read and short-read assembly, metatranscriptomic RNA-seq, 16S/18S/ITS amplicon denoising, and downstream MAG analysis including binning, annotation, taxonomy, and metabolic profiling. Assembly pipelines produce a FASTA + depth table that feeds directly into mag_analysis; illumina_rna consumes those same assembly/MAG FASTAs as mapping references.

├── nanopore_live/          Real-time analysis during sequencing
│   │                       11 modules, 16 processes -> DuckDB
│
├── nanopore_assembly/      Long-read assembly + mapping + depth

│   │                       Flye/metaMDBG/myloasm -> minimap2 -> CoverM
│   │                       Output: assembly.fasta + depths.txt + BAMs
│
├── illumina_assembly/      Multi-assembler consensus + mapping + depth
│   │                       7 modules: preprocess, error_correct, normalize,
│   │                       merge_reads, assembly, dedupe, mapping
│   │                       Output: assembly.fasta + depths.txt + BAMs
│
├── illumina_amplicon/      Amplicon (16S/18S/ITS) denoising to ASVs
│   │                       11 modules: primers, demultiplex, denoise, merge,
│   │                       taxonomy, phylogeny, renormalize, metadata,
│   │                       cluster, network, shiny
│   │                       cutadapt -> papa2 (DADA2) -> MAFFT/FastTree
│   ├── viz/                Interactive Svelte dashboard (ASV explorer)
│   └── bin/                Pipeline scripts
│
├── illumina_rna/           Metatranscriptomic RNA-seq vs references
│   │                       5 modules: preprocess, rrna, alignment, quantify, summarize

│   ├── viz/                Interactive Svelte dashboard (gene-expression heatmap)

docs.title: BYOBAM: supply the polishing alignment instead of letting Flye build it
docs.text: Status: proposal. The Flye side already exists upstream; the pipeline side does not.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
Timings from the marine co-assembly (8.9 Gbp, 1,176,983 contigs, 250 Gbp reads, 192-core node, work dir on Lustre):

phase wall-clock minimap2 alignment + sort 52 min samtools index -c -@ 4 5h53m separating alignment into bubbles 2h04m correcting bubbles 2h53m polish total 11h42m

The alignment is not the problem. Indexing is half the wall-clock, at roughly 4 MB/s over an 85 GB BAM, on four threads hardcoded in flye/polishing/alignment.py. Lustre contention makes it worse -- the freshwater assembly was writing its own 96 GB BAM over the same window.

Separately, MAP_READS then maps every sample against the polished assembly: 276 tasks, each rebuilding a split minimap2 index over the same 8.9 Gbp reference, ~1.5 h and 48 GB peak per task. That is a second full mapping pass over reads Flye has already aligned.

docs.title: What Flye already supports
docs.text:
flye --polish-target accepts a BAM in place of reads:

  • flye/main.py sets bam_input when a reads argument ends in .bam
  • flye/polishing/polish.py then skips make_alignment entirely
  • and, critically, does not delete the file: if not bam_input: os.remove(alignment_file)

Constraints, both enforced in main.py and both already satisfied by the pipeline: a single BAM only, and --iterations 1.

So Flye does not need patching for this. The alignment simply becomes ours.

docs.title: Proposed shape
docs.text:
PREPARE_READS ──► all_reads.fastq + read_map.tsv.gz
                        │
                  MAP_TO_DRAFT            one minimap2 over the draft assembly,
                        │                 our threads, sort --write-index,
                        │                 work dir on node-local scratch
                        ├──► FLYE_POLISH --polish-target draft.fasta aln.bam
                        │                 (skips its own mapping and indexing)
                        └──► DEMUX_BAM    split by read_map into per-sample BAMs
                                          published to mapping/ as today

MAP_READS stays for metaMDBG, myloasm and --polish false, where no such alignment exists.

docs.title: What it buys
docs.text:
• removes the 5h53m index pass: samtools sort --write-index writes the CSI during sorting (samtools >= 1.10; danaSeq pins >= 1.17 in the flye env, and Flye now prefers a PATH samtools over its vendored 1.9)
  • removes the second mapping pass entirely (276 tasks, ~1.5 h, 48 GB each)
  • removes the failure mode those tasks caused: on the marine run 116 task failures across 39 of 276 samples, each retried once then silently ignored, leaving 14% of samples absent from the depth matrix
  • one alignment, one set of flags, used for both polishing and coverage

docs.title: What it costs / open questions
docs.text:
• Coordinates are the draft, not the polished assembly. Contig names are identical (normalize_assembly.py renumbers before polishing and Flye preserves names), so all binners are unaffected -- they work per contig and match by name. Only CALCULATE_GENE_DEPTHS is coordinate-sensitive, and its sole consumer is viz. Accepted 2026-09-20.
  • Read set differs from today's MAP_READS. The polish alignment is post-dedupe, post-filtlong, post-REMOVE_HUMAN; MAP_READS maps the raw per-barcode reads. Arguably an improvement, but it is a change.
  • Flye's own flags differ from MAP_READS. Flye emits -N 10 -p 0.5 --secondary-seq; MAP_READS uses --secondary=no. If we own the alignment we choose, but the polisher wants secondaries and coverm does not -- so the demux must filter -F 0x100, as the prototype already does.
  • Disk. The alignment must survive from mapping through polishing and demultiplexing; 85 GB for marine, 96 GB for freshwater. Node-local scratch is the right home (and would likely have avoided the 4 MB/s index), but it has to outlive a single process, not a single task.
  • Validation still outstanding. Demuxed depths have not yet been compared against a full MAP_READS run. The marine run that would have provided the baseline was cancelled because 39 samples were missing; a re-run with the corrected memory label (danaSeq 2ad6fb7) would provide it.

docs.title: The other samtools cost: per-region spawns
docs.text:
BYOBAM removes the indexing pass, but not this one, because it lives inside Flye's polishing loop regardless of who built the alignment.

Flye calls samtools in six places:

site call frequency alignment.py:265 view -T ref -u - once (pipe stage) alignment.py:266 sort -@ 4 -l 1 -m MEM once alignment.py:277 index -c -@ 4 once -- 5h53m on marine sam_parser.py:358 depth -r ctg:s-e -a -m 0 -Q 10 -l 100 per region sam_parser.py:378 view bam ctg:s-e per region sam_parser.py:443 view bam (whole file) once

SynchonizedChunkManager emits one region per contig, and both make_bubbles and consensus drive it. On the marine assembly that is 1,176,983 subprocess spawns; freshwater's BAM has 1,325,561 references.

Measured on fir, samtools 1.22, page-cache warm:

samtools view -H <96.7 GB bam>   ->  0.59 s, 364 MB RSS
header size                      ->  40,032,496 bytes / 1,325,561 @SQ records

Every region query pays that before reading a single alignment:

1,325,561 regions x 0.59 s ~= 217 core-hours of pure header parsing

which across 128 workers is ~1.7 h of wall-clock -- close to the 2h04m observed for bubbles, and again for consensus (2h53m).

Newer samtools helps, but does not fix this: - samtools depth was rewritten in 1.13 and is materially faster - htslib >= 1.10 hashes reference names; older paths did linear scans, which is pathological at 1.3M refs - BGZF threading improved, which matters for sort/index given more than 4 threads - but the 0.59 s above IS 1.22. A newer binary cannot fix re-parsing a 40 MB header 1.3M times.

The fix is architectural: batch many regions per invocation (samtools view accepts multiple regions, or -M -L regions.bed), or hold one reader open per worker instead of forking per contig. Batching 1000 contigs per spawn would cut header parses ~1000x. This only bites assemblies with very many contigs -- i.e. exactly the metagenome case, and not the isolate case Flye was tuned for.

docs.title: Prototype status
docs.text: demux_bam_by_sample.py splits a pooled BAM by read_map.tsv.gz. Verified 120/120 on synthetic data with known ground truth, and 108/108 correct with zero misassignments on the real marine polishing BAM. Read maps for both habitats are built and validated (marine 276 samples / 97,363,917 reads; freshwater 232 / 87,815,882) -- every read in every staged file is accounted for, because the sample comes from the filename rather than the header.

docs.title: danaSeq illumina_amplicon
docs.text:
Amplicon sequencing analysis pipeline — from raw reads to interactive visualization

danaSeq illumina_amplicon is a Nextflow DSL2 pipeline for amplicon sequencing analysis. It takes demultiplexed paired-end FASTQ files and produces ASV tables, multi-database taxonomy, phylogenies, ordinations, and correlation networks.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Denoising is papa2 (a DADA2 port: filter, dereplicate, denoise, merge, chimera removal, taxonomy). Everything downstream — QC filtering, ordination, networks, visualization — is carried by this stage's own scripts in bin/.

Raw FASTQ files
    │
    ├── REMOVE_PRIMERS (cutadapt)
    ├── DADA2_FILTER_TRIM (papa2)
    ├── DADA2_LEARN_ERRORS (papa2, per-plate)
    ├── DADA2_DENOISE (papa2, per-plate)
    ├── MERGE_SEQTABS
    ├── REMOVE_CHIMERAS (papa2)
    ├── FILTER_SEQTAB (bin/)
    │
    ├── ASSIGN_TAXONOMY (papa2, parallel per DB)
    ├── BUILD_PHYLOGENY (bin/ + MAFFT)
    ├── RENORMALIZE (bin/)
    │
    ├── ORDINATE (bin/, t-SNE/PCA)
    ├── NETWORK (bin/, SparCC)
    └── EXPORT_VIZ (bin/, JSON → Svelte)

docs.title: Illumina Assembly Pipeline
docs.text: Multi-assembler pipeline for Illumina paired-end metagenomic reads. Pools the contigs of four assemblers and deduplicates them, and produces the deduplicated assemblies with depth tables and BAMs for downstream MAG analysis.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
cd illumina_assembly
./install.sh && ./install.sh --check

# Local (conda)
./run-illumina-assembly.sh --input /path/to/reads --outdir /path/to/output

# Co-assembly mode
./run-illumina-assembly.sh --input /path/to/reads --outdir /path/to/output --coassembly

# Apptainer (HPC) -- auto-pulls SIF on first run
./run-illumina-assembly.sh --apptainer --pull --input /path/to/reads --outdir /path/to/output

# SLURM profile
./run-illumina-assembly.sh --input /path/to/reads --outdir /path/to/output \
    -profile slurm --slurm_account def-myaccount \
    --conda_path ~/scratch/miniforge3/bin

docs.title: Pipeline Stages
docs.text: Step Process Tool Description 1 CLUMPIFY BBTools clumpify Optical deduplication 2 FILTER_BY_TILE BBTools filterbytile Remove low-quality tiles 3 BBDUK_TRIM BBDuk Adapter trimming (k=23, mink=11, minlen=70) 4 BBDUK_FILTER BBDuk Artifact + PhiX removal (k=31, entropy=0.95) 5 REMOVE_HUMAN BBTools removehuman Human read removal (optional) 6 FASTQC FastQC QC report on preprocessed reads (optional) 7 ERROR_CORRECT_ECCO BBMerge ecco Phase 1: overlap-based error correction 8 ERROR_CORRECT_ECC BBTools clumpify ecc Phase 2: clump-based error correction (4 passes) 9 ERROR_CORRECT_TADPOLE Tadpole Phase 3: k-mer-based error correction (k=62) 10 NORMALIZE_READS bbnorm Coverage normalization (target=100, mindepth=2) 11 MERGE_READS BBMerge Merge overlapping pairs (k=93) 12 QUALITY_TRIM BBDuk Quality-trim unmerged reads 13a ASSEMBLE_TADPOLE Tadpole Assembly (k=124) 13b ASSEMBLE_MEGAHIT Megahit Assembly (k=45-225) 13c ASSEMBLE_SPADES SPAdes Assembly (k=25-125) 13d ASSEMBLE_METASPADES metaSPAdes Assembly (k=25-77, --meta) 14 DEDUPE_ASSEMBLIES BBTools dedupe Cascade deduplication (100% -> 99% -> 98%) 15 MAP_READS_BBMAP BBMap Map QC'd reads to assembly (minid=90) 16 CALCULATE_DEPTHS jgi_summarize_bam_contig_depths Depth matrix in MetaBAT2 format

docs.title: Required
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --input (required) Directory containing paired-end *_R1_*.fastq.gz files --outdir results Output directory

docs.title: Mode
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --coassembly false Co-assemble all samples together

docs.title: Preprocessing
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --min_readlen 70 Minimum read length after trimming --run_remove_human true Remove human reads via removehuman.sh --human_ref <repo>/../databases/human_ref Path to BBTools human reference index; must exist when --run_remove_human is true --run_fastqc true Run FastQC on final preprocessed reads --run_normalize true Enable bbnorm coverage normalization

docs.title: Assembly
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --run_tadpole true Run Tadpole assembler --run_megahit true Run Megahit assembler --run_spades true Run SPAdes assembler --run_metaspades true Run metaSPAdes assembler --run_mapping true Map reads back to the deduplicated assembly and compute depths; false stops after deduplication --dedupe_identity 98 Final deduplication identity threshold --min_contig_len 500 Minimum contig length after deduplication

docs.title: Resources
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --assembly_cpus 24 CPUs for assembly processes --assembly_memory 250 GB Memory for assembly processes --workdir $SLURM_TMPDIR/illumina_assembly_work, else /tmp/... Nextflow work directory. Node-local by default under Slurm: read intermediates and SPAdes' k-mer temp files stay off the shared filesystem and vanish with the job; use --store_dir to keep outputs for resume

docs.title: SLURM
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --slurm_account (none) SLURM --account for job submission; required with -profile slurm --conda_path (none) Path to conda/mamba bin/ for SLURM jobs

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
results/
├── preprocess/<sample>/        QC'd reads + FastQC reports
├── error_correct/<sample>/     Three-phase error-corrected reads
├── normalize/<sample>/         Coverage-normalized reads + k-mer histograms
├── merge/<sample>/             Merged + quality-trimmed reads
├── assembly/<sample>/
│   ├── <sample>.dedupe.fasta   Final deduplicated assembly
│   ├── <sample>.tadpole.fasta  Per-assembler outputs
│   ├── <sample>.megahit.fasta
│   ├── <sample>.spades.fasta
│   ├── <sample>.metaspades.fasta
│   └── <sample>.assembly_stats.txt
├── mapping/<sample>/
│   ├── <sample>.sorted.bam     Alignments
│   ├── <sample>.sorted.bam.bai BAM index
│   ├── <sample>.depths.txt     Depth matrix (MetaBAT2 format)
│   └── <sample>.covstats.txt   Per-contig coverage statistics
└── pipeline_info/              Nextflow reports (timeline, trace, DAG)

In co-assembly mode the assembly and the depth table are published under coassembly (assembly/coassembly/coassembly.dedupe.fasta, mapping/coassembly/coassembly.depths.txt), but each sample's BAM is still published under its own mapping/<sample>/ directory. mag_analysis --bam_dir reads a single directory, so for a co-assembly the BAMs have to be collected into one directory by hand.

Feed these outputs into mag_analysis:

cd ../mag_analysis
./run-mag-analysis.sh \
    --assembly results/assembly/<sample>/<sample>.dedupe.fasta \
    --depths results/mapping/<sample>/<sample>.depths.txt \
    --bam_dir results/mapping/<sample>/ \
    --outdir /path/to/analysis --db_dir /path/to/databases

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text: Profile Use case standard Local execution (default) test Small test data, reduced resources (4 CPUs, 8 GB) slurm SLURM cluster execution

docs.title: Resource Requirements
docs.text:
Defaults from nextflow.config; process_high is --assembly_cpus / --assembly_memory. The first five preprocessing steps scale with the size of their input instead of using a label, so small samples do not each reserve the whole assembly allocation.

Process Label CPUs RAM Notes CLUMPIFY, FILTER_BY_TILE (input-scaled) 4 + 2 per GB of input, capped at --assembly_cpus 8 GB + 16 GB per GB of input, capped at --assembly_memory Per sample BBDUK_TRIM, BBDUK_FILTER (input-scaled) 4 + 2 per GB 8 GB + 8 GB per GB, capped Per sample REMOVE_HUMAN (removehuman.sh) (input-scaled) 8 + 2 per GB 32 GB + 8 GB per GB, capped Loads the masked human index FASTQC, QUALITY_TRIM, CALCULATE_DEPTHS process_medium 8 24 GB 4 h Error correction (three phases), NORMALIZE_READS, MERGE_READS process_high 24 250 GB 24 h; per sample Tadpole, Megahit, SPAdes, metaSPAdes, DEDUPE_ASSEMBLIES process_high 24 250 GB 24 h; SPAdes/metaSPAdes is the most memory-intensive step MAP_READS_BBMAP process_high 24 250 GB 24 h; per sample

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
--input must point to a directory containing paired-end Illumina reads:

input_dir/
├── sampleA_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz
├── sampleA_S1_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz
├── sampleB_S2_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz
├── sampleB_S2_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz
└── ...

R2 files are matched by replacing _R1_ with _R2_. The sample ID is extracted as the first field before _ in the filename.

docs.title: Design Notes
docs.text:
• Multi-assembler approach. Four assemblers capture different k-mer ranges. Cascade deduplication (100% -> 99% -> 98%) merges them into a single non-redundant contig set.
  • Three-phase error correction. Overlap-based (bbmerge ecco), clump-based (clumpify ecc, 4 passes), and k-mer-based (tadpole ecc k=62) correction each catch different error types.
  • Human decontamination. Enabled by default via BBTools' removehuman.sh. Disable with --run_remove_human false.
  • Interleaved read handling. BBTools operates on interleaved FASTQ throughout, simplifying channel plumbing.
  • Graceful assembler failure. All assemblers use set +e and produce an empty FASTA on error. The deduplication step skips empty files.
  • SRA-safe. Automatic fallbacks for SRA-stripped read headers that lack optical duplicate coordinates.

docs.title: Illumina RNA Pipeline
docs.text: Paired-end Illumina RNA-seq pipeline tailored for metatranscriptomic data mapped against references from other danaSeq pipelines (assemblies from illumina_assembly/nanopore_assembly, or annotated MAGs from mag_analysis).

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
cd illumina_rna
./install.sh && ./install.sh --check

# Local (conda)
./run-illumina-rna.sh \
    --input /path/to/reads \
    --references /path/to/refs_dir \
    --outdir /path/to/output \
    --human_ref /path/to/bbtools_human_index \
    --sortmerna_refs /path/to/sortmerna_fastas

# Apptainer (HPC) -- auto-pulls SIF on first run
./run-illumina-rna.sh --apptainer --pull \
    --input /path/to/reads --references /path/to/refs --outdir /path/to/output

# SLURM profile
./run-illumina-rna.sh --input /path/to/reads --references /path/to/refs --outdir /path/to/output \
    -profile slurm --slurm_account def-myaccount \
    --conda_path ~/scratch/miniforge3/bin

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• --input — directory of paired-end reads. Supports two naming conventions:
    • Illumina: *_R1_*.fastq.gz / *_R2_*.fastq.gz
    • BGI/MGI: *_1.fq.gz / *_2.fq.gz (and *.fastq.gz variants)
  • --references — directory of <name>.fasta files. If a sibling <name>.gff is present (typically the output of bakta/prokka annotation), gene-level counts are emitted via featureCounts; otherwise quantification is contig-level only via samtools idxstats.

docs.title: Pipeline Stages
docs.text: Step Process Tool Description 1 CLUMPIFY BBTools clumpify Optical deduplication 2 FILTER_BY_TILE BBTools filterbytile Bad-tile filtering 3 BBDUK_TRIM BBTools bbduk Adapter trimming + length filter 4 BBDUK_FILTER BBTools bbduk Artifact + PhiX removal 5 REMOVE_HUMAN BBTools removehuman Host decontamination (optional) 6 FASTQC FastQC Per-sample QC report (optional) 7 REMOVE_RRNA SortMeRNA rRNA depletion (optional, on by default) 8 BBMAP_INDEX BBMap Reference index build 9 MAP_READS_BBMAP BBMap + samtools Per-(sample, reference) alignment 10 FEATURECOUNTS subread featureCounts Gene-level counts (when GFF provided) 11 MERGE_GENE_COUNTS python/pandas Genes × samples matrix per reference 12 VIZ_PREPROCESS python JSONs for the Svelte viz

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
results/
├── preprocess/<sample>/                Cleaned reads + FastQC + SortMeRNA log
├── mapping/<sample>/<ref>/             sorted.bam(.bai), idxstats, flagstat, covstats
├── quantify/<sample>/<ref>/            featureCounts per-sample counts + summary
├── expression/<ref>/                   <ref>.gene_counts.tsv (merged, genes × samples)
├── viz/                                JSONs for the Svelte viz
└── pipeline_info/                      Nextflow timeline/report/trace/dag

docs.title: Viz
docs.text:
cd viz
npm install
VIZ_DATA_DIR=/path/to/output/viz npm run dev
# open http://localhost:5173

Pages: Overview (sample × reference mapping-rate matrix, read-flow funnel), Samples (per-sample read flow + per-reference mapping detail), Expression (top-variance gene × sample heatmap with log₂ transform; per-reference dropdown), References (per-contig read totals).

docs.title: MAG Analysis Pipeline
docs.text: Technology-agnostic downstream analysis for metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs). Accepts a pre-computed assembly + depth table from any assembler and runs binning, annotation, taxonomy, metabolic profiling, mobile genetic element detection, eukaryotic analysis, ecosystem services mapping, phylogenetics, and interactive visualization.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
cd mag_analysis
./install.sh && ./install.sh --check

# Basic run
./run-mag-analysis.sh \
    --assembly /path/to/assembly.fasta \
    --depths /path/to/depths.txt \
    --outdir /path/to/output \
    --annotator bakta --db_dir /path/to/databases

# All modules
./run-mag-analysis.sh \
    --assembly /path/to/assembly.fasta \
    --depths /path/to/depths.txt \
    --bam_dir /path/to/mapping/ \
    --outdir /path/to/output \
    --all --db_dir /path/to/databases

# Apptainer (HPC)
./run-mag-analysis.sh --apptainer \
    --assembly /path/to/assembly.fasta \
    --depths /path/to/depths.txt \
    --outdir /path/to/output \
    --all --db_dir /path/to/databases

docs.title: Binning
docs.text: Step Process Tool Description 1a BIN_SEMIBIN2 SemiBin2 Self-supervised contig binning (needs BAMs) 1b BIN_METABAT2 MetaBAT2 Depth + TNF binning (always runs) 1c BIN_MAXBIN2 MaxBin2 EM-based abundance binning 1d BIN_LORBIN LorBin Long-read-aware binning (needs BAMs) 1e BIN_COMEBIN COMEBin Contrastive learning binning (needs BAMs) 1f BIN_VAMB VAMB Variational autoencoder binning 1g BIN_VAMB_TAX VAMB Taxonomy-guided variational autoencoder binning 2a DASTOOL_CONSENSUS DAS Tool Score-based consensus of multiple binners 2b BINETTE_CONSENSUS Binette CheckM2-guided bin refinement 2c MAGSCOT_CONSENSUS MAGScoT Marker-gene-based consensus 3 CHECKM2 CheckM2 Completeness and contamination assessment 3b DEREP_GALAH galah + skani Species-level dereplication of the consensus bins, ranked by CheckM2

docs.title: Annotation
docs.text: Step Process Tool Description 4a PROKKA_ANNOTATE Prokka ORF prediction + functional annotation 4b BAKTA_BASIC Bakta CDS annotation (lightweight) 4c BAKTA_EXTRA Bakta Full-database annotation (CDS, sORFs, expert systems; rRNA/tRNA/ncRNA and CRISPR are skipped) 4d BAKTA_EXTRA_IDS Python Renames BAKTA_EXTRA features to the BAKTA_BASIC locus tag of the CDS at the same coordinates, since all protein tools run on the basic proteins; sORFs get new tags after the last basic one. docs.title: Protein reference databases
docs.text:
--protein_db_dir DIR (with --run_metabolism; --db_dir resolves <db_dir>/protein_dbs) searches the annotation proteins against every database in DIR, one subdirectory per database. The layout is the one nanopore_live's --pollutant_dbs reads, so one directory serves both pipelines:

File Meaning <name>/<name>.hmm HMM profiles, searched with hmmsearch <name>/<name>.dmnd DIAMOND database, searched with diamond blastp (best hit per protein) <name>/<name>.genes.tsv Optional catalogue: target gene category pathway subpathway description [threshold score_type motif] <name>/<name>.opts Optional cutoff: tc, ga, nc or an E-value for HMMs, optionally followed by resolve; id=,qcov=,scov=,evalue=,len=,bits= for DIAMOND

Without an .opts file, HMMs use --hmm_cut (default tc), or the catalogue's per-target thresholds when <name>.genes.tsv has a threshold column; DIAMOND uses --protein_db_opts. Each database's hits are in metabolism/protein_dbs/<name>/<name>.protein_db.tsv, and merged_annotations.tsv gains a protein_db_hits column (<db>:<gene>, comma-separated). The results are stored per database, so adding one later searches only that one; after changing a database or its .opts, delete its metabolism/protein_dbs/<name>/ to search it again.

An HMM search over more than --protein_db_chunk proteins (default 50,000) is split into chunks searched in parallel, 4 hmmsearch threads per chunk, since one hmmsearch gains little from more threads. E-values are computed against the whole protein set, so the hits are those of a single search. Give the step the node with --protein_db_cpus: on 72,231 proteins PGAP took ~2.2 CPU-hours and the full CATH FunFam library ~8.7, and both scale with total protein length.

With resolve (e.g. 1e-3 resolve), the per-domain hits go through cath-resolve-hits, and only each protein's best non-overlapping set of models is kept. This is for libraries of overlapping families, such as CATH FunFam, where one protein otherwise matches dozens of related models.

./download-databases.sh --funfam writes <db_dir>/protein_dbs/CATH-FunFam/: CATH FunFam v4.3.0 (212,872 models), searched at 1e-3 resolve; --funfam-superfamilies 3.40.50.300,1.10.8 keeps only some superfamilies.

./download-databases.sh --pgap writes <db_dir>/protein_dbs/PGAP/: NCBI's PGAP HMMs, which hold the maintained TIGRFAMs (accessions TIGR*) plus NCBIfam and PRK models, searched at their noise cutoffs (nc; the trusted cutoffs NCBI uses for genomes are often too strict for metagenomes).

docs.title: MetaCyc pathways
docs.text:
With --metacyc_db (and --metacyc_refs), mag_analysis predicts which MetaCyc pathways each DAS Tool MAG, and the community as a whole, carries. It does not run Pathway Tools on your data. Proteins get MetaCyc reactions through Rhea: DIAMOND hits to Rhea-annotated UniProtKB proteins, plus Bakta/eggNOG EC numbers and KofamScan/eggNOG KOs. Pathways are then called with PathoLogic's published rules (Karp et al. 2011, doi:10.4056/sigs.1794338). Those rules are permissive, so every call carries a confidence value built from its evidence:

  • each reaction is weighted by its strongest evidence: a DIAMOND hit scores 0.5 at 35% identity rising to 1.0 at 80%; EC-only and KO-only evidence score 0.45; an EC mapped straight to a MetaCyc reaction without a Rhea link scores 0.30
  • confidence is the mean weight over the pathway's reactions (0-1)
  • tier high means confidence >= 0.7, at least half of the present reactions backed by a sequence hit, every key reaction sequence-backed, and the MAG not outside the pathway's MetaCyc taxonomic range; medium means confidence >= 0.35; everything else is low

How reliable the tiers are. The high-tier cut-offs (confidence 0.7 and the taxonomic-range condition) were fitted against EcoCyc, the hand-curated E. coli K-12 database, with E. coli MG1655 run through mag_analysis; the weights are the original estimates. For base (non-super) pathways that exist in MetaCyc:

Tier Share of calls that are curated EcoCyc pathways Share of curated pathways called in this tier high 0.79 0.54-0.68 medium 0.29-0.38 0.18-0.29 low 0.04-0.07 0.02-0.03

Ranges span runs with the full reference and with every Escherichia, Enterobacteriaceae or Enterobacterales protein removed from it, which is closer to a MAG from a novel genus. With 20-60% of the genes removed (an incomplete MAG) the high tier stayed at 0.75-0.79 precision and its recall fell to 0.18-0.53. Super-pathways are less reliable (high tier ~0.64), because they are called whenever all their components are. Treat low-tier calls as possibilities rather than findings. tools/metacyc_benchmark.py reruns the comparison for any curated PGDB you have (export, compare, degrade); see its --help. The step needs Bakta annotation (--annotator bakta). It is skipped, with one log line, when --metacyc_db is not given.

Getting MetaCyc. MetaCyc is licensed by SRI International and is never downloaded automatically. You need one of:

You have Where it comes from MetaCyc flat files (a tarball or directory containing pathways.dat, reactions.dat, classes.dat) a BioCyc subscription (flat-file download for MetaCyc) the Pathway Tools Linux installer (pathway-tools-XX.X-linux-64-tier1-install) a Pathway Tools licence from SRI (free for academic use) an existing Pathway Tools Apptainer image (.sif), e.g. from MetaPathways build_pt your site

Setup (once per site):

./download-databases.sh --db_dir /path/to/databases --metacyc-refs          # open references
./download-databases.sh --db_dir /path/to/databases --metacyc <tarball|dir|installer|.sif>
# installer on an Apptainer-only host (e.g. an HPC cluster): give the MetaPathways image as the runtime
apptainer pull mp.sif docker://quay.io/hallamlab/metapathways:4.0.3
./download-databases.sh --db_dir /path/to/databases --metacyc pathway-tools-30.0-linux-64-tier1-install \
    --metacyc-runtime mp.sif
Step Writes Time Disk --metacyc-refs <db_dir>/metacyc_refs/: Rhea, KEGG ko->reaction, GTDB r226->NCBI taxids, and the DIAMOND reference (Swiss-Prot plus one Rhea-annotated protein per UniRef90 cluster, 9.4M sequences) ~1 h, mostly downloads (UniProt idmapping 7 GB; TrEMBL ~40 GB is streamed through a filter, never stored) ~15 GB scratch at peak, 5.5 GB kept --metacyc (flat files) <db_dir>/metacyc/ seconds ~140 MB --metacyc (installer or .sif) <db_dir>/metacyc/, exported in batch mode from a temporary Pathway Tools install ~3 min 3.5 GB temporary

The installer runs as your own user, with no root, inside the Pathway Tools runtime that ships in the MetaPathways image, and the install is deleted afterwards. <db_dir>/metacyc/ is created owner-only and carries a VERSION.json (MetaCyc release, source, date).

Licence. Keep <db_dir>/metacyc/ private. Don't put it in container images, git repositories or shared or public locations. The pipeline outputs carry MetaCyc pathway and reaction identifiers and names, so share them under the same terms as MetaCyc itself.

--db_dir finds <db_dir>/metacyc and <db_dir>/metacyc_refs automatically. Taxonomic-range rules use GTDB-Tk's classification (--run_gtdbtk). Without GTDB-Tk they use SendSketch contig calls (--run_sendsketch), which are less reliable, and the log says so; with neither, the range rules are off. Without them the high tier is less precise (0.73 instead of 0.79 on the EcoCyc benchmark). --metacyc_taxonomy sendsketch forces the SendSketch calls; none turns the range rules off.

Outputs in metabolism/metacyc/:

  • metacyc_pathways.tsv: one row per bin (plus _community) and pathway with any evidence: the call and the rule that decided it, confidence and confidence_tier, reaction counts by evidence (n_seq, n_ec_only, n_ko_only, n_ec_direct_only, n_linked_only: reactions credited only through a link to a sequence-supported reaction that shares a complete EC number or a MetaCyc enzyme), sequence identity, key and unique reaction support, up to 12 supporting hits (reaction=protein:UniProt:identity), and a MinPath-style parsimony flag (minpath)
  • metacyc_reactions.tsv.gz: one row per protein and MetaCyc reaction, with its evidence classes, DIAMOND identity, coverage and hit, and the ECs and KOs behind it
  • metacyc_bin_taxonomy.tsv: each bin's GTDB lineage and the NCBI taxids used for the taxonomic ranges
  • metacyc_hits.tsv.gz: the DIAMOND hits

On 72,231 proteins (7 MAGs), the DIAMOND search took 21 min on 8 threads with a 17 GB peak (sensitive, -b 2), and the scorer took 14 s and 0.6 GB. For a co-assembly of ~13M proteins, expect the search to take ~1.5-2.5 h on a 192-CPU node (--metacyc_cpus 192; raise --metacyc_block_size to 4-6 and --metacyc_memory to ~96 GB for fewer passes over the reference). The scorer then takes ~20 min, ~5 GB, and as much scratch in its work dir as the input tables. Results do not depend on --metacyc_chunk; a smaller value only lowers memory.

docs.title: Dereplication
docs.text:
--run_derep clusters the consensus bins (DAS Tool, plus Binette and MAGScoT when they run) at species-level ANI with galah, and keeps one representative per cluster: the genome with the highest completeness − 5 × contamination, less small penalties for contig count and ambiguous bases (galah's Parks2020_reduced). It needs --checkm2_db, and clusters only bins that CheckM2 scored. Within one run, it picks the best of the refiners' versions of each genome; it does not dereplicate across runs or co-assemblies.

binning/derep/derep_clusters.tsv lists every consensus bin. Its status is representative, member (with its skani ANI and aligned fractions against the representative; NA if the pair falls below skani's 80% ANI screen), failed_quality (outside the completeness/contamination thresholds), or no_checkm2 (no CheckM2 estimate, e.g. a bin above --checkm2_max_bin_bp).

Note: the bin-size cut-offs --binette_min_bin_bp, --binette_max_bin_bp, --checkm2_max_bin_bp and --gtdbtk_max_bin_bp are compared against the bin FASTA's size in bytes, which approximates its length in bp (headers and line breaks included). --derep_min_size_bp counts sequence bases.

Parameter Default Description --run_derep false Dereplicate the consensus bins with galah (needs --checkm2_db) --derep_ani 95 ANI (%) at which genomes are clustered --derep_min_af 15 Minimum aligned fraction (%) for two genomes to cluster --derep_min_completeness 50 CheckM2 completeness (%) below which a bin is not clustered --derep_max_contamination 10 CheckM2 contamination (%) above which a bin is not clustered --derep_min_size_bp 500000 Bins shorter than this (bp) are not clustered, so a fragment cannot become a representative

docs.title: Design Notes
docs.text:
• Seven-binner consensus. SemiBin2, MetaBAT2, MaxBin2, LorBin, COMEBin, VAMB, VAMB-tax feed into DAS Tool + Binette + MAGScoT for consensus refinement.
  • Modular activation. MetaBAT2, DAS Tool, Bakta annotation (--annotator bakta) and ECOSSDB (--run_ecossdb, when metabolism runs) are on by default; every other module is off until enabled with its --run_* flag, or with the launcher's --all.
  • Technology-agnostic. Accepts assemblies from Nanopore, Illumina, HiFi, or any external assembler. Only requires FASTA + MetaBAT2-format depth table.
  • Persistent caching. Use --store_dir to skip completed processes across runs, even after work/ cleanup.
  • Quality tiers. The viz preprocessing tiers MAGs from CheckM2 completeness/contamination as HQ (>=90%, <5%), MQ (>=50%, <10%) or LQ; the MIMAG rRNA/tRNA criteria are not applied.

docs.title: Reference Mapping
docs.text:
Map nanopore reads against arbitrary reference genomes via minimap2 (ONT preset). Used by the AIS page in the SPA to surface invasive species detection, but the module is generic — any reference works.

The pipeline takes a directory of references (--mapping_refs) and fans out across every reference it finds. Each per-barcode dana.duckdb gains a mapping table keyed on reference (the reference name), so downstream tools (the SPA's preprocess_ais.py, ad-hoc duckdb queries, etc.) can pull per-sample stats with a single WHERE reference = '...'.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
nextflow run nanopore_live/main.nf \
    --input        /path/to/run \
    --outdir       /data/scratch/nanopore_live/<run-id> \
    --mapping_refs /matika/projects/project_zebra/refs \
    --run_db_integration --danadir nanopore_live/bin \
    -resume

Drop a new refs/<name>/ directory with <name>.idx + meta.json and the next pipeline run picks it up automatically. No code changes needed. References are enumerated once at start-up, so a running watch-mode pipeline must be restarted (-resume) to map against a newly added reference.

docs.title: Reference directory layout
docs.text:
<refs_dir>/
└── <reference_name>/
    ├── <reference_name>.fna          # source fasta (or multifasta)
    ├── <reference_name>.idx          # minimap2 ONT preset index — required
    ├── <reference_name>.contigs.json # linear contig offsets (SPA preprocess)
    ├── meta.json                     # human-readable labels (SPA preprocess)
    └── source.txt                    # free-text provenance (optional)

<reference_name> is the canonical handle. Keep it lowercase, alnum, no spaces — it becomes:

  • the mapping.reference value in dana.duckdb;
  • the output filename in each barcode dir (map/<input file>/<name>.txt);
  • the SPA JSON filename (ais_<name>.json);
  • the species id in the SPA's AIS_SPECIES list.

Examples: zebramussel, quaggamussel, sealamprey, roundgoby.

docs.title: Adding a new reference
docs.text: The end-to-end workflow has five short steps. Examples use sea lamprey; substitute REFNAME and ACC for your target.

docs.title: 1. Acquire the fasta
docs.text:
REFNAME=sealamprey
ACC=GCF_048934315.1     # RefSeq / GenBank accession
REFDIR=/matika/projects/project_zebra/refs/$REFNAME
mkdir -p "$REFDIR" && cd "$REFDIR"

# NCBI datasets API → zip → extract the genomic fasta
curl -sS --fail -o ncbi.zip \
  "https://api.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/v2/genome/accession/$ACC/download?include_annotation_type=GENOME_FASTA"
FNA_PATH=$(unzip -l ncbi.zip | awk '/_genomic\.fna$/ {print $4}' | head -1)
unzip -p ncbi.zip "$FNA_PATH" > "$REFNAME.fna"
rm ncbi.zip

For species with no whole-genome assembly (e.g. some AIS invertebrates), fall back to a multifasta of all GenBank records under the taxon:

TAXID=77747
ES=$(curl -sS "https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi?db=nuccore&term=txid${TAXID}[Organism]&usehistory=y&retmax=0")
WENV=$(echo "$ES" | grep -oP '<WebEnv>\K[^<]+')
QK=$(echo  "$ES" | grep -oP '<QueryKey>\K[^<]+')
curl -sS "https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?db=nuccore&WebEnv=$WENV&query_key=$QK&rettype=fasta&retmode=text" \
  > "$REFNAME.fna"

Detection sensitivity is then limited to whatever regions are covered by those markers — typically COI / 18S / mitochondrion. Note this in meta.json.notes so future-you remembers.

docs.title: 2. Build the minimap2 index
docs.text:
The pipeline requires a pre-built .idx (memory-mapping a 4 GB index per task is much faster than rebuilding it 600× per pipeline run):

minimap2 -d "$REFDIR/$REFNAME.idx" "$REFDIR/$REFNAME.fna"

If you want to use a non-ONT preset, build the index with that preset's flags here — the pipeline only invokes minimap2 -ax map-ont against the .idx, but minimap2 picks up most index-time parameters from the .idx itself.

docs.title: 3. Build the contig offset map
docs.text:
The SPA's per-sample position histogram needs to know how to linearise hits across multiple contigs. build_contig_index.py writes a small JSON sidecar:

python3 /matika/projects/project_zebra/build_contig_index.py "$REFDIR/$REFNAME.fna"
# → writes $REFDIR/$REFNAME.contigs.json

Resulting shape: 

{
  "total_length": 1808348452,
  "contigs": [
    {"name": "NC_133667.1", "length": 37671560, "offset": 0},
    {"name": "NC_133668.1", "length": 29380143, "offset": 37671560},
    ...
  ]
}

docs.title: 4. Write the helper file meta.json
docs.text:
The pipeline itself doesn't need meta.json (it uses the directory name as the canonical ID). The SPA preprocess reads it to label markers / species cards.

{
  "id": "sealamprey",
  "species": "Petromyzon marinus",
  "common_name": "Sea lamprey",
  "category": "AIS",
  "accession": "GCF_048934315.1",
  "assembly_name": "UKy_Petmar_22M1.pri1.0",
  "assembly_level": "Chromosome",
  "source": "NCBI Datasets API",
  "added": "2026-05-27",
  "notes": "Free-form. Close native sister taxa, recommended HQ cutoffs, etc."
}
Field Required Used by Notes id yes SPA Must match directory + .idx basename species yes SPA Latin binomial; rendered italicised common_name yes SPA UI label category no SPA Future grouping (e.g. AIS, pathogen, host) accession recommended docs NCBI/RefSeq accession assembly_name, assembly_level recommended docs Provenance source recommended docs Where the fasta came from added recommended docs ISO date notes recommended docs Cross-mapping caveats, recommended HQ cutoff, etc.

docs.title: 5. Run the pipeline
docs.text:
Once <refs_dir>/<name>/<name>.idx exists, point the pipeline at <refs_dir> and re-run (a watch-mode run must be restarted; the reference list is read at start-up):

nextflow run nanopore_live/main.nf \
    --input        /path/to/run \
    --outdir       /data/scratch/nanopore_live/<run-id> \
    --mapping_refs <refs_dir> \
    --run_db_integration --danadir nanopore_live/bin \
    -resume

Outputs land at: - Per-barcode : <outdir>/<FC>/<BC>/map/<input file>/<refname>.txt (filtered SAM-ish: mapq≥1, aligned_len≥10; one subdir per input FASTQ chunk) - DuckDB : <outdir>/<FC>/<BC>/dana.duckdb → table mapping (loaded by import_all.py → import_mapping)

docs.title: 6. Surface in the SPA
docs.text:
Edit nanopore_live/viz/src/views/AISView.svelte:

const AIS_SPECIES = [
  { id: 'zebramussel', label: 'Zebra mussel', latin: 'Dreissena polymorpha' },
  { id: 'sealamprey',  label: 'Sea lamprey',  latin: 'Petromyzon marinus' },
  // ... add new id here. Must match meta.json `id` exactly.
];

Then run preprocess_ais.py to aggregate the per-barcode duckdb rows into the SPA-shaped JSON:

DPY=nanopore_live/conda-envs/dana-tools/bin/python
$DPY preprocess_ais.py \
    --reference $REFNAME \
    --species   "$(jq -r .species     refs/$REFNAME/meta.json)" \
    --common    "$(jq -r .common_name  refs/$REFNAME/meta.json)" \
    --contigs   refs/$REFNAME/$REFNAME.contigs.json \
    --output    <preprocess_dir>/ais_$REFNAME.json

Then viz/deploy.sh to push to microscape.app.

docs.title: HAB compound references
docs.text:
The same mapping_refs plumbing powers the SPA's /habs view for cyanobacterial HAB compound BGC detection. Differences vs. AIS:

  • Each ref is a biosynthetic gene cluster (full BGC fasta with intergenic regions, not just CDS) named after the chemical compound: microcystin, cylindrospermopsin, saxitoxin, anatoxin_a, nodularin.
  • The fasta concatenates the BGC from multiple producer taxa per compound (e.g. microcystin.fna contains the mcy cluster from Microcystis, Planktothrix, Anabaena/Dolichospermum, …) so a hit reflects bloom potential regardless of which producer is present. The per-producer offsets are surfaced as ticks on the position histogram.
  • meta.json uses category: "HAB" and adds compound (chemical name)
  • class (chemistry / syndrome class, e.g. cyclic heptapeptide) in place of species / common_name.
  • Preprocess: run preprocess_habs.py (sister to preprocess_ais.py) to emit hab_<id>.json:
$DPY preprocess_habs.py \
    --reference $REFNAME \
    --compound  "$(jq -r .compound refs/$REFNAME/meta.json)" \
    --class     "$(jq -r .class    refs/$REFNAME/meta.json)" \
    --contigs   refs/$REFNAME/$REFNAME.contigs.json \
    --output    <preprocess_dir>/hab_$REFNAME.json
  • SPA: nanopore_live/viz/src/views/HABsView.svelte mirrors AISView (same Leaflet + identity + position histograms, amber accent instead of emerald). Add new compounds to HAB_COMPOUNDS there; id must match the ref dirname / .idx basename / hab_<id>.json filename.

docs.title: Standalone scripts (no Nextflow)
docs.text:
For one-off batches outside the pipeline:

Script What it does /matika/projects/project_zebra/run-nanopore-mapping.sh Walks out_dana_bc/<FC>/<BC>/fq/, runs minimap2, writes map/<refname>.txt to scratch. Args: REFERENCE_INDEX_PATH. /matika/projects/project_zebra/load_mapping_to_duckdb.py Walks the scratch tree, appends to each barcode's dana.duckdb. Same mapping table, same import_log key. Idempotent. /matika/projects/project_zebra/build_contig_index.py Writes <name>.contigs.json from <name>.fna. /matika/projects/project_zebra/preprocess_ais.py Aggregates duckdb → ais_<name>.json for the SPA.

The pipeline integration uses the same mapping schema; its import_log key is the per-chunk path map/<input file>/<refname>.txt (the flat map/<refname>.txt layout written by the standalone script is the older layout — see the note in import_mapping.py).

docs.title: DuckDB schema
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE mapping (
    reference    TEXT,      -- e.g. 'zebramussel'
    qname        TEXT,      -- read id
    flag         INTEGER,
    rname        TEXT,      -- target sequence
    pos          INTEGER,
    mapq         INTEGER,
    cigar        TEXT,
    nm           INTEGER,   -- NM tag (edit distance)
    as_score     INTEGER,   -- AS tag
    de           REAL,      -- minimap2 gap-compressed divergence (de:f:)
    identity_pct REAL,      -- (1 - de) * 100
    aligned_len  INTEGER
);

Useful aggregations:

-- Per-reference summary across all barcodes (run inside one dana.duckdb)
SELECT reference,
       COUNT(*)                 AS hits,
       ROUND(AVG(identity_pct), 2) AS mean_id,
       SUM(CASE WHEN identity_pct > 90 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS hq_hits,
       ROUND(AVG(mapq), 1)      AS mean_mapq
FROM mapping
GROUP BY reference;

docs.title: Nanopore Assembly Pipeline
docs.text: Long-read metagenomic assembly pipeline for Oxford Nanopore data. Preprocesses reads, runs assembly with selectable assemblers, maps reads back to contigs, and produces depth tables for downstream MAG analysis.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
cd nanopore_assembly
./install.sh && ./install.sh --check

# Local (conda)
./run-nanopore-assembly.sh --input /path/to/reads --outdir /path/to/output

# Choose assembler
./run-nanopore-assembly.sh --input /path/to/reads --outdir /path/to/output --assembler metamdbg

# Apptainer (HPC)
./run-nanopore-assembly.sh --apptainer --input /path/to/reads --outdir /path/to/output

# Docker
./run-nanopore-assembly.sh --docker --input /path/to/reads --outdir /path/to/output

docs.title: Pipeline Stages
docs.text: Step Process Tool Description 1 CONCAT_READS cat Concatenate per-barcode FASTQs into one file per sample 2 PREPARE_READS fastq_filter Pooling, read-ID deduplication, size selection (--filtlong_size), nano-hq quality check 3 REMOVE_HUMAN minimap2 Remove human-mapped reads (optional) 4a FLYE_ASSEMBLE Flye --meta Long-read metagenome assembly (default) 4b ASSEMBLY_METAMDBG metaMDBG Minimizer-space de Bruijn graph assembly (alternative) 4c ASSEMBLY_MYLOASM myloasm Hybrid overlap/DBG assembly (alternative) 5 FLYE_POLISH Flye Assembly polishing iterations (optional, default for Flye) 6 MAP_READS minimap2 + samtools Per-sample alignment to assembly (flag -F 0x104: drops unmapped and secondary, keeps supplementary) 7 CALCULATE_DEPTHS CoverM Coverage depth table in MetaBAT2 format 8 CALCULATE_TNF tetramer_freqs (C) 136-feature tetranucleotide frequency profiles

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --input (required) Directory containing *.fastq.gz or fastq_pass/barcode*/ structure --outdir results Output directory --assembler flye Assembler: flye, metamdbg, or myloasm --read_type (required for flye) Flye read mode: nano-raw, nano-hq or nano-corr; auto is accepted with a warning --min_overlap 1000 Flye --min-overlap parameter --polish (auto) Run Flye polisher; auto-enabled for Flye, disabled for others --dedupe true Read-ID deduplication before assembly (awk per barcode, fastq_filter across the pool) --filtlong_size (skip) Filtlong target bases (e.g. 40000000000); skip if not set --min_barcode_size 10485760 Skip barcodes with fewer than 10 MB of reads --run_remove_human true Remove human reads via minimap2 --human_ref <repo>/../databases/human_ref/GRCh38_noalt_as.fa.gz Path to human reference FASTA or .mmi; must exist when --run_remove_human is true --assembly_cpus 16 CPUs for assembly processes --assembly_memory 60 GB Memory for assembly processes --store_dir (none) Persistent cache directory (storeDir)

docs.text:
results/
├── assembly/
│   ├── assembly.fasta          Co-assembly
│   ├── assembly_info.txt       Contig metadata (length, coverage, circularity)
│   ├── assembly_graph.gfa      Assembly graph
│   ├── tnf.tsv                 Tetranucleotide frequencies (136 features)
│   └── gc.tsv                  Per-contig GC content
├── mapping/
│   ├── <sample>.sorted.bam     Per-sample alignments
│   ├── <sample>.sorted.bam.bai BAM indices
│   └── depths.txt              CoverM depth matrix (MetaBAT2 format)
└── pipeline_info/
    ├── timeline.html           Execution timeline

    ├── trace.txt               Per-process trace

    └── versions.yml            Tool versions and parameters

Feed these outputs into mag_analysis:

cd ../mag_analysis
./run-mag-analysis.sh \
    --assembly /path/to/results/assembly/assembly.fasta \
    --depths /path/to/results/mapping/depths.txt \
    --bam_dir /path/to/results/mapping/ \
    --outdir /path/to/analysis --db_dir /path/to/databases

Defaults from nextflow.config; process_high is --assembly_cpus / --assembly_memory.

Process Label CPUs RAM Notes CONCAT_READS process_medium 8 16 GB Per barcode; up to 32 in parallel PREPARE_READS (fastq_filter) process_high 16 60 GB Single pooled task REMOVE_HUMAN (minimap2) process_high 16 60 GB minimap2 against GRCh38 Flye / metaMDBG / myloasm assembly, Flye polish process_high 16 60 GB Scales with metagenome complexity MAP_READS (minimap2) process_medium 8 >= 24 GB Per sample; memory scaled to the assembly size (at least 24 GB, doubled on retry) CALCULATE_DEPTHS (CoverM) process_low 2 4 GB Operates on all BAMs CALCULATE_TNF, PUBLISH_UNPOLISHED process_low 2 4 GB

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
Nanopore barcode directory structure (MinKNOW output):

input_dir/
├── fastq_pass/
│   ├── barcode01/*.fastq.gz
│   ├── barcode02/*.fastq.gz
│   └── ...

Or a flat directory of FASTQ files:

input_dir/
├── sample1.fastq.gz
├── sample2.fastq.gz
└── ...

Barcodes with fewer than --min_barcode_size bytes (default 10 MB) are automatically skipped.

docs.title: Design Notes
docs.text:
• Multiple assemblers. Flye (default), metaMDBG, and myloasm each handle different read quality profiles. Select with --assembler.
  • CoverM depth calculation. Uses CoverM instead of MetaBAT2's jgi_summarize_bam_contig_depths to avoid integer overflow with supplementary alignments.
  • Human decontamination. Enabled by default via minimap2 against GRCh38. Disable with --run_remove_human false.
  • Tetranucleotide frequencies. 136-feature TNF profiles computed by a compiled C binary for downstream binning and visualization.
  • Persistent caching. Use --store_dir to skip completed processes across runs, even after work/ cleanup.
  • Auto-polishing. Polishing is automatically enabled for Flye assemblies and disabled for metaMDBG/myloasm. Override with --polish true/false.

docs.title: Real-Time Nanopore Pipeline
docs.text: Real-time metagenomic analysis for Oxford Nanopore sequencing data. Processes reads as they stream from MinKNOW, providing live taxonomic classification, gene annotation, and functional profiling.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
cd nanopore_live
./install.sh && ./install.sh --check

./run-realtime.sh --input /path/to/nanopore/run --outdir /path/to/output \
    --run_kraken --kraken_db /path/to/krakendb \
    --annotator bakta --bakta_db /path/to/bakta/db-light --run_sketch --run_tetra

docs.title: Pipeline Stages
docs.text: Step Process Tool Description 1 VALIDATE_FASTQ gzip + fastq_gz_salvage.py Gzip integrity check; damaged files salvaged record by record 2 QC_FASTQ_FILTER fastq_filter (C++) Length + quality filtering (streaming, Filtlong-style scoring) 3 CONVERT_TO_FASTA awk Header cleanup and format conversion 4a KRAKEN2_CLASSIFY Kraken2 Taxonomic classification (batched per sample) 4b PROKKA_ANNOTATE Prokka ORF prediction + functional annotation 4c BAKTA_CDS / BAKTA_FULL Bakta CDS-only or full annotation (default annotator) 4d HMM_SEARCH HMMER3 Profile HMM search against user-supplied / pollutant databases 4e DIAMOND_DB_SEARCH DIAMOND blastp of annotation proteins against .dmnd databases 4f SENDSKETCH BBTools Per-read GTDB classification via a sendsketch server 4g TETRAMER_FREQ tetramer_freqs (C) Tetranucleotide composition profiles 4h MAP_REFERENCE minimap2 (ONT) Per-reference alignment for AIS / custom genomes — see mapping-references.md 5 DB_INTEGRATION Python + DuckDB Load all results into DuckDB (batch mode) 6 DB_SYNC Python + DuckDB Periodic sync, dashboard preprocess and deploy hook during watch mode 7 CLEANUP bash Delete imported source files after DB import

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --input (required) Directory containing fastq_pass/ --outdir results Output directory --run_kraken false Enable Kraken2 classification --kraken_db (required if kraken) Path to Kraken2 database --annotator bakta Gene annotator: prokka, bakta, or none --bakta_db /data/scratch/refdbs/bakta/db-light Path to Bakta database (site-specific default) --bakta_full false Run full Bakta annotation (ncRNA/tRNA/CRISPR) --hmm_databases (skip) Comma-delimited paths to HMM files --hmm_cut tc hmmsearch cutoff (tc/ga/nc/E-value); per-DB <name>.opts overrides --protein_dbs (skip) Comma-delimited DIAMOND .dmnd paths --protein_db_opts id=50,qcov=50,scov=50,evalue=1e-5 DIAMOND cutoffs --pollutant_dbs (skip) Directory of <name>/<name>.hmm|.dmnd pollutant databases --mapping_refs (skip) Directory of reference subdirs for minimap2 mapping (AIS / custom) — see mapping-references.md --run_sketch false Enable per-read GTDB sendsketch classification --sendsketch_address $DANA_SENDSKETCH_ADDRESS, else http://localhost:3068/sketch Sendsketch server URL --run_tetra false Enable tetranucleotide frequency --watch false Monitor for new files during live sequencing (watch globs are auto-detected from the depth of fastq_pass/ below --input) --db_sync_minutes 10 DuckDB sync interval in watch mode --run_db_integration false Load results into DuckDB --cleanup false Delete imported files after DB import --metadata (none) Sample metadata TSV passed to the dashboard preprocess --min_readlen 1500 Minimum read length after filtering --keep_percent 80 Percent of reads to keep (by quality) --min_file_size 1000000 Minimum FASTQ file size in bytes (1 MB) --store_dir (none) Persistent cache directory (storeDir)

├── FLOWCELL/
│   ├── barcode01/
│   │   ├── fa/           FASTA (quality-filtered sequences)
│   │   ├── kraken/       *.tsv (per-read), *.report (summary)

docs.title: Read map (t-SNE of every read)
docs.text:
In watch mode, DB_SYNC runs viz/preprocess/compute_read_tsne.py whenever tetra_data grows. With fastsne installed every read is mapped, not a sample. The container ships both builds and uses the GPU one whenever a GPU is visible: run-realtime.sh --docker passes --gpus all when Docker has the NVIDIA runtime, and an Apptainer run needs --nv. Without a GPU it runs fastsne_cpu. install.sh installs both into dana-tools from the pinned fastsne release (self-contained binaries: the GPU one needs only the NVIDIA driver, 525 or newer).

  • each sample's tetra_data is exported once to viz/read_map/fsb/ (re-exported only when its dana.duckdb changes)
  • a reference t-SNE is built from a uniform random sample of up to --ref-max reads (10M on CPU, 20M on a GPU) and rebuilt when the read count has doubled (--rebuild-factor)
  • the other reads are projected onto it, only for samples whose data changed
  • viz/read_explorer.json keeps a --max-reads sample for the dashboard, with coordinates from the full map
  • viz/read_map/viewer.html?data=reads.json shows every read (WebGL, paged), coloured by kraken genus, sample or distance to the reference; projected reads can be hidden

On a GPU, mapping every read of a 173M-read collection takes about 13 minutes (V100-class card). fastsne_cpu uses half the available cores by default (--threads), leaving room for basecalling and classification. Without fastsne, or with --engine sklearn, the sampled sklearn t-SNE runs as before.

docs.text: Profile Use case standard Local execution test Lower size/length thresholds (no test data are bundled) shipboard Production workstation: 32 CPUs, 256 GB RAM, 100 GB Kraken2 local_tools Legacy: conda disabled, tools expected on PATH

docs.title: Resource Requirements
docs.text:
Defaults from nextflow.config (batch / watch mode):

Component CPUs RAM Notes Kraken2 4 / 1 10 GB (100 GB in shipboard) Depends on database size; serialized via maxForks=1 Bakta (BAKTA_CDS) all cores / 1 16 GB / 4 GB Batch: one task at a time; watch: one task per core minimap2 (MAP_REFERENCE) 1 4 GB At most 16 / 4 concurrent tasks Other process_medium tasks (Prokka, HMMER3, sendsketch, DB sync) 1 4 GB Other process_low tasks (QC, DIAMOND, tetramers) 1 2 GB

docs.title: Watch Mode
docs.text:
Monitor a directory for new FASTQ files during active sequencing:

./run-realtime.sh --input /path/to/runs --outdir /path/to/output \
    --watch --db_sync_minutes 10 \
    --run_kraken --kraken_db /path/to/db \
    --annotator bakta --run_db_integration

DB_SYNC runs as a long-lived process that periodically loads new results into DuckDB. The Python loader (bin/import_all.py) is idempotent and tracks imports via import_log. Watch vs batch mode is locked per --outdir (recorded in <outdir>/.pipeline_mode).

docs.title: Post-DB Cleanup
docs.text:
The --cleanup flag compresses or deletes source files after DuckDB import:

Directory/Files Action kraken/, sketch/, tetra/ (except tetra/*.lengths) Delete (data lives in DuckDB) prokka/*/PROKKA_*.tsv, bakta/*/*.tsv Delete (loaded into DuckDB) fa/*.fa, .gff/.gff3, .faa, .ffn Kept uncompressed (Nextflow publishDir would re-copy them on -resume) hmm/, protdb/, map/, dana.duckdb Kept (not cleaned)

Cleanup runs only for barcode directories whose import_log is non-empty (i.e. after at least one successful import).

docs.title: DuckDB Integration
docs.text:
bin/import_all.py <barcode_dir> loads all results into the per-barcode dana.duckdb in one process:

Step Data import_kraken, import_krakenreport Kraken2 per-read classifications and summary reports import_annotations Bakta/Prokka gene annotations, stats, read-contig mapping import_sketch Sendsketch per-read GTDB classifications import_tetra Tetranucleotide frequencies + sequence index import_mapping.py minimap2 hits into the mapping table import_protein_hits.py HMM / DIAMOND protein-DB hits db_schema.py Shared schema definitions

The loader is idempotent and tracks imports via import_log. The legacy R scripts in bin/ (47_merge_db.r etc.) are not called by the pipeline.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
Oxford Nanopore directory structure with multiplexed barcodes:

input_dir/fastq_pass/
├── barcode01/*.fastq.gz
├── barcode02/*.fastq.gz
└── ...

docs.title: Design Notes
docs.text:
• Kraken2 batching. In batch mode, FASTAs are grouped per sample (groupTuple) so the DB loads once per barcode. In watch mode, files stream individually. Uses maxForks = 1 since Kraken2 loads 50-100 GB into RAM.
  • Compiled C tools. fastq_filter (QC) and tetramer_freqs (TNF) are compiled C binaries in bin/, replacing filtlong and a Python script.
  • Watch mode. Uses Channel.watchPath() with a flat glob pattern (Java WatchService limitation -- no recursive **).
  • Conda environments. Four isolated environments avoid dependency conflicts: dana-bbmap, dana-prokka, dana-bakta, dana-tools.

docs.title: Container
docs.text: Pre-built container images include Nextflow, papa2, cutadapt, MAFFT, and FastTree — everything needed to run the full pipeline without installing dependencies.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
# Pull the image
docker pull ghcr.io/rec3141/danaseq-illumina-amplicon:latest

# Run the pipeline
docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/data ghcr.io/rec3141/danaseq-illumina-amplicon \
    run /pipeline/main.nf \
    --input /data/reads \
    --ref_databases "silva:/data/silva.fasta:Domain,Phylum,Class,Order,Family,Genus" \
    --outdir /data/results \
    -resume

docs.title: Apptainer (HPC)
docs.text:
# Pull and convert to SIF
apptainer pull danaseq-illumina-amplicon.sif docker://ghcr.io/rec3141/danaseq-illumina-amplicon:latest

# Run the pipeline through the image entrypoint (`run`, not `exec`: the
# entrypoint loads /pipeline/docker.config, which turns conda off so the
# tools already on PATH are used)
apptainer run danaseq-illumina-amplicon.sif run /pipeline/main.nf \
    --input /path/to/reads \
    --ref_databases "silva:/path/to/silva.fasta:Domain,Phylum,Class,Order,Family,Genus" \
    --outdir results \
    -resume

docs.title: Launcher
docs.text:
run-illumina-amplicon.sh does the above for you: it picks Apptainer > Singularity > Docker > local conda, pulls the image if needed (--pull, or --sif PATH for a pre-built SIF), binds --outdir and --input, forwards the host CA bundle, and appends -resume:

cd danaSeq/illumina_amplicon
./run-illumina-amplicon.sh --runtime apptainer \
    --input /path/to/reads \
    --ref_databases "silva:/path/to/silva.fasta:Domain,Phylum,Class,Order,Family,Genus"

There are no docker/singularity Nextflow profiles in this pipeline.

docs.title: What's Inside
docs.text:
The container includes:

Component Version Source Nextflow latest nextflow.io papa2 v1.0.1 (pinned tag in envs/python.yml, bumped deliberately) GitHub release via pip cutadapt latest bioconda MAFFT + FastTree latest bioconda

There is no R in the image: papa2 is byte-identical to R dada2 1.40 (see its parity documentation), so the pipeline runs on one engine.

docs.title: Building Locally
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/rec3141/danaSeq.git
cd danaSeq
docker build -t danaseq-illumina-amplicon illumina_amplicon

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
All parameters can be set via command line (--param value) or in a params file.

nextflow run main.nf --help

docs.title: Input / Output
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --input required Directory of paired-end *.fastq.gz files --outdir results Output directory --store_dir off Persistent cache directory (skip completed steps across runs)

docs.title: Primer Removal
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --skip_primer_removal false Skip removal; the reads already have their primers off --primers_fwd detect Forward primer FASTA, applied to R1 (overrides detection) --primers_rev detect Reverse primer FASTA, applied to R2 (overrides detection) --primer_detect_reads 500 Reads sampled per file when detecting primers --primer_error_rate 0.12 Cutadapt max error rate

docs.title: DADA2 Quality Filtering
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --maxEE 2 Max expected errors per read --truncQ 2 Truncate at first base with quality <= Q --maxN 0 Max Ns allowed --truncLen_fwd 0 Truncate forward reads at position N (0 = off) --truncLen_rev 0 Truncate reverse reads at position N (0 = off) --min_overlap 12 Minimum overlap for paired-read merging

docs.title: QC Filtering
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --min_seq_length 50 Remove ASVs shorter than N bp --min_samples 2 Remove ASVs present in fewer than N samples --min_seqs 3 Remove ASVs with fewer than N total reads --min_reads 100 Remove samples with fewer than N reads

docs.title: Taxonomy
docs.text:
Parameter Default Description --ref_databases required Reference databases, semicolon-separated: "name:path:Level1,Level2,..." --taxonomy_seed 100 RNG seed for the taxonomy bootstraps (fixed for reproducible confidence values) --run_phylogeny false Build MSA + FastTree phylogenetic tree

Example: 

--ref_databases "silva:/db/silva_nr99_v138.1_train_set.fa.gz:Domain,Phylum,Class,Order,Family,Genus;pr2:/db/pr2_train.fasta:Domain,Supergroup,Division,Class,Order,Family,Genus,Species"

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --metadata off Path to MIMARKS-compliant TSV/CSV metadata file --sample_id_column sample_name Column name in metadata matching sample IDs

docs.title: Network
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --min_prevalence 5 Min samples (a count) an ASV must appear in for network analysis

docs.title: Resources
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --denoise_cpus 8 CPUs for the process_high steps (error learning, denoising, chimera removal, taxonomy, phylogeny, network) --denoise_memory 16 GB Memory for the process_high steps

docs.title: Stage A: Preprocessing and DADA2
docs.text:
Step Process Tool Description 1 DEMULTIPLEX Mr_Demuxy Optional inner-barcode demultiplexing 2 REMOVE_PRIMERS cutadapt Primer trimming (auto-selects by 16S/18S/ITS prefix) 3 FILTER_TRIM papa2 Per-sample quality filtering (maxEE, truncQ, PhiX) 4 LEARN_ERRORS papa2 Per-plate error model learning (LOESS) 5 DENOISE papa2 Denoising, pair merging, per-plate chimera removal 6 MERGE_SEQTABS papa2 Merge per-plate tables (long-format) 7 REMOVE_CHIMERAS papa2 Chimera removal on merged data (pooled by default; --chimera_method) 8 FILTER_SEQTAB filter_seqtab.py Length, prevalence, abundance, and depth filtering

Per-plate processing

Steps 3–5 run independently per plate (samples sharing PCR history). This allows per-plate error learning while scaling to hundreds of plates.

docs.title: Stage B: Taxonomy, Phylogeny, and Normalization
docs.text:
Step Process Tool Description 9 ASSIGN_TAXONOMY papa2 Naive Bayesian classification (parallel per ref DB) 10 BUILD_PHYLOGENY build_phylogeny.py + MAFFT + FastTree MSA + FastTree tree (optional, --run_phylogeny) 11 RENORMALIZE renormalize.py Group ASVs by taxonomy, normalize within groups

Multiple databases

Supply multiple reference databases with --ref_databases and taxonomy is assigned against each in parallel. Results are merged in the output.

docs.title: Stage C: Ordination, Networks, and Visualization
docs.text: Step Process Tool Description 12 LOAD_METADATA load_metadata.py Sample metadata integration (MIMARKS) 13 CLUSTER_TSNE cluster_tsne.py Bray-Curtis + t-SNE ordination (samples and ASVs) 14 NETWORK_SPARCC network_sparcc.py CLR + Pearson co-occurrence network (not the SparCC algorithm) 15 BUILD_VIZ build_viz.py JSON export for Svelte web viewer

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
The pipeline uses long-format DataFrames as its canonical representation from the merge step onward:

sample          sequence            count
plate1_A01      TACGGAGGATGCGA...   1523
plate1_A01      TACGGAGGATCCGA...   847
plate1_A02      TACGGAGGATGCGA...   2041

This avoids materializing a dense matrix (samples × ASVs), which can exceed memory for large datasets (4K+ samples, 100K+ ASVs).

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
Profile Description standard Local executor (default) slurm Submit each task as a Slurm job test Reduced resources for CI/testing

Conda environments (envs/python.yml) are created automatically; there is no conda profile. Container execution goes through run-illumina-amplicon.sh (see Container); there are no docker/singularity profiles.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Nextflow >= 23.04
  • Conda or Mamba (environments are created automatically when running outside a container)
  • Or: Docker / Apptainer (for container execution)

The pipeline lives in illumina_amplicon/ of the repository; there is no root main.nf, so it is run from a local clone.

docs.title: Run from Local Clone
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/rec3141/danaSeq.git
cd danaSeq/illumina_amplicon

nextflow run main.nf \
    --input /path/to/reads \
    --ref_databases "silva:/path/to/silva.fasta:Domain,Phylum,Class,Order,Family,Genus" \
    -resume

docs.title: Run with Container
docs.text:
The launcher picks Apptainer > Singularity > Docker > local conda, binds --outdir and --input, and appends -resume:

cd danaSeq/illumina_amplicon

./run-illumina-amplicon.sh \
    --input /path/to/reads \
    --ref_databases "silva:/path/to/silva.fasta:Domain,Phylum,Class,Order,Family,Genus"

# Force a runtime
./run-illumina-amplicon.sh --runtime apptainer --input /path/to/reads ...

See Container for the image and for running it without the launcher.

docs.title: Multi-Database Taxonomy
docs.text:
Classify against multiple reference databases in parallel:

nextflow run main.nf \
    --input /path/to/reads \
    --ref_databases "silva:/db/silva.fasta:Domain,Phylum,Class,Order,Family,Genus;pr2:/db/pr2.fasta:Domain,Supergroup,Division,Subdivision,Class,Order,Family,Genus,Species" \
    --run_phylogeny \
    -resume

The first database named is the primary one: renormalization groups, the per-ASV lineage strings and the viewer's default labels come from it.

docs.title: Persistent Cache
docs.text:
For large projects, use --store_dir to skip completed steps across runs:

nextflow run main.nf \
    --input /path/to/reads \
    --ref_databases "silva:/db/silva.fasta:Domain,Phylum,Class,Order,Family,Genus" \
    --store_dir /scratch/danaseq_amplicon_cache \
    -resume

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
Results are written to --outdir (default: results/):

results/
├── demultiplexed/         Demultiplexed reads (--run_demultiplex only)
├── trimmed/               cutadapt logs, detected primers (detected/), primer assignment
├── quality_check/         Per-sample auto-trim and per-group truncation policy tables
├── filtered/              Filter/trim statistics
├── error_models/          Per-group error models and plots
├── seqtabs/               Per-group sequence tables
├── seqtab_final/          Merged, chimera-filtered and QC-filtered tables and stats
├── taxonomy/              Per-database classifications
├── phylogeny/             Alignment + FastTree tree (--run_phylogeny)
├── renormalized/          Per-group proportional tables
├── clustering/            t-SNE coordinates (samples and ASVs)
├── network/               Correlation edge list and stats
├── viz/                   JSON data for the web viewer (+ tree.nwk, run_manifest.json)
├── site/                  Built static viewer (--build_viz_site)
└── pipeline_info/         Nextflow timeline, report, trace, DAG, pipeline_timing.tsv

With --store_dir, the per-sample intermediates (demultiplexed/, filtered/, error_models/, seqtabs/, cutadapt logs) go to the cache directory instead of --outdir.
